title: Fppf presentations and restriction of quotient groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A groupoid in algebraic spaces means objects $U$ and arrows $R$ with source $s$, target $t$, unit $e$, inverse and composition giving groupoids on all test-scheme points, naturally under pullback; for schemes these are [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. For such a groupoid, $[U/R]$ denotes the fppf stackification [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], [def-pc-fppf-site] of the presheaf of groupoids $T\mapsto(U(T),R(T))$. (1) If $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], the diagonal of $[U/R]$ is representable by algebraic spaces and $U\to[U/R]$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Its self 2-fibre product is canonically $R$, with projections $s,t$. (2) If $a:U\to\mathcal Z$ is a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme map to an algebraic stack, the self-relation groupoid $R=U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ has flat locally finitely presented projections, and its canonical map $[U/R]\to\mathcal Z$ is an equivalence commuting with $a$. (3) If a groupoid $(U,R)$ is the restriction of a groupoid $(V,Q)$ along a surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme map $q:U\to V$, meaning $R\cong(U\times_SU)\times_{V\times_SV}Q$ with all operations induced, then $[U/R]\to[V/Q]$ is an equivalence commuting with the canonical maps from $U$ and $V$. Algebraic space means [def-trf-algebraic-space], and all representable properties are tested on scheme charts; surjectivity means field-extension local lifting. An algebraic stack means an etale stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas (equivalently its fppf-stack convention, by [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]); stack, 2-fibre products and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts after a field extension.

source.place: Tag 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation), with spaces-groupoids.tex Tags 04M9 (lemma-quotient-stack-2-cartesian), 046S (lemma-quotient-stack-restrict) and 046T (lemma-quotient-stack-restrict-equivalence). proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] to the groupoid of clause (1). Its hypotheses are precisely that $U,R$ are algebraic spaces, their operations form groupoids on test schemes, and $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. It gives the representable diagonal, the representable surjective flat locally finitely presented object map, and the specified arrow-map equivalence $R\simeq U\times_{[U/R]}U$. The projections are $s,t$ by that statement. This proves clause (1), using an existing stronger theorem; we do not need its additional smooth-atlas conclusion.

For clause (2), $\mathcal Z$ is an fppf stack by [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]: its etale stack, representable diagonal and smooth surjective scheme atlas are exactly the hypotheses of that node. Apply [lem-sfb-self-relation-quotient-embedding] to $a:U\to\mathcal Z$ (regarding the scheme $U$ as its algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]). It gives the algebraic space $R$, the self-relation groupoid, and a fibrewise fully faithful $i:[U/R]\to\mathcal Z$ with specified $i\pi\simeq a$. Each projection $R\to U$ is a scheme base change of $a$; hence it is flat and locally of finite presentation by the hypothesis on $a$, whose meaning is the stated scheme-base-change test. The inverse and composition are inversion and composition of the displayed isomorphisms in $\mathcal Z$, as the cited self-relation node specifies.

source.place: Tag 04T4 (lemma-map-space-into-stack), parts (1), (4)-(6); Tag 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation). Fppf-stack convention: criteria.tex Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale).

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and $z\in\mathcal Z(T)$. Representability of $a$ gives an algebraic space $F=U\times_{\mathcal Z}T$, and $F\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by the same test. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $W\to F$, allowed by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] with target chart $T\to T$, the scheme map $W\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. It is surjective: a point $t\in T$ gives $z_t$ over $\kappa(t)$; surjectivity of $a$ lifts it up to isomorphism to an element of $U(L)$ for some field extension $L/\kappa(t)$. This is an element of $F(L)$, which lifts to the surjective chart $W$ after a further field extension. Thus every $t$ is in the image of $W\to T$. Consequently $\{W\to T\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. Its tautological element of $F(W)$ is a map $u:W\to U$ and an isomorphism $a(u)\simeq z|_W$.

source.place: Tag 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation), the local-lifting argument of Tag 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation), with spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03MM and 0410 (chart tests).

proof.text: The objects $\pi(u)$ of step 3 map under $i$ to $z$ locally, since $i\pi\simeq a$. The source is an fppf stack by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] and the target is an fppf stack by step 2. The functor $i$ is fibrewise fully faithful by step 2. Therefore [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence], applied on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site], makes $i$ an equivalence. The already specified $i\pi\simeq a$ proves the required compatibility. This finishes clause (2).

For clause (3), the morphism on groupoid points sends $u$ to $q(u)$ and an arrow to its specified image in $Q$. Because all operations on $R$ are induced from $Q$, these maps form a pullback-compatible functor between the two groupoid prestacks. Composing with the target stackification and applying the extension clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] gives $j:[U/R]\to[V/Q]$ and a specified isomorphism $j\pi_U\simeq\pi_Vq$. For $u,v:T\to U$ the arrow presheaf in the first groupoid is $T\times_{(u,v),U\times_SU,(s,t)}R$; in the second it is $T\times_{(qu,qv),V\times_SV,(s,t)}Q$. The restriction isomorphism in the hypothesis identifies these presheaves, respecting their maps to the two stackifications. They are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], hence fppf sheaves by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The Isom clause of stackification identifies their sheafifications with the Isom sheaves of the corresponding image objects. Sheafifying either of these sheaves fixes it, by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Thus $j$ induces an isomorphism of Isom sheaves on these object pairs.

For arbitrary $x,y\in[U/R](T)$, the local-object clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] puts both in the form $\pi_U(u),\pi_U(v)$ on an fppf covering (take a common covering using the site axioms of [def-pc-fppf-site]). Conjugation by the chosen isomorphisms reduces the map of their Isom sheaves to step 5. A map of sheaves which is an isomorphism on a covering is an isomorphism: injectivity follows by restriction and sheaf uniqueness; for surjectivity take local inverse images, whose restrictions agree on overlaps by local injectivity, and glue them by the sheaf axiom. Hence the map on Isom sets over $T$ is bijective. This proves fibrewise full faithfulness of $j$, without assuming flatness or local finite presentation of the source and target maps of either groupoid.

source.place: Tag 046S (lemma-quotient-stack-restrict), fppf-local test on Isom sheaves.

proof.text: For $z\in[V/Q](T)$, [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] gives an fppf covering on which $z\simeq\pi_V(v)$ for a map $v:T_i\to V$. Pull back the given fppf scheme covering $q:U\to V$ along $v$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], $W_i=T_i\times_VU\to T_i$ is an fppf covering. Its tautological map $u:W_i\to U$ satisfies $qu=v|_{W_i}$, so $j\pi_U(u)\simeq z|_{W_i}$ by step 5. This is local essential surjectivity (successive coverings suffice by the site axioms [def-pc-fppf-site]). Both quotients are fppf stacks by the stackification node, and step 6 gives full faithfulness. Thus [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] makes $j$ an equivalence. The specified $j\pi_U\simeq\pi_Vq$ is exactly the compatibility with the two canonical maps. This proves clause (3).
